take_homes: The AI fills gaps with typical, plausible text, and it is too kind when it grades its own work. A person who knows the subject has to be the check.
What you learn can be saved as a rules file, and that file can be improved and shared. This is how a habit could move from one person to a team.
Ask the agent for a plan and approve it before it changes files.

monday.move: Pick my onboarding challenge for Module 2 and write the three-line handoff file. Before anything else I will ask the DPO and works council rep whether any HR material can go into an AI tool.
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO says no employee data, I use only non-personal material and keep going
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I have not asked yet.

misconception.why: The module never talked about roles, hiring or headcount. It was about making one page and saving rules. It did show that the AI needs a knowledgeable person to check it, which is a small point against my idea, but not enough to change my mind.

one_line: The exercise taught me that the AI is too kind to its own work, which I'll remember. But the same filler paragraph appeared fourteen times and nobody said what this means for people's jobs.
